blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: scope — Where a name is accessible
local — Declared in a limited scope
class field — Variable belonging to a class/object
shadowing — Inner name hides an outer name

blocks.title: Explain the important decision
blocks.text: The class field and method-local variable are different storage locations. C# allows a local to hide a field; this does not permit redeclaring any local in a nested block.

blocks.title: Worked example · Spot two variables with one name
blocks.text: class Program { static int score = 10; static void Main() { int score = 3; System.Console.WriteLine(score); System.Console.WriteLine(Program.score); } }

blocks.title: Worked example · Identify both variables
blocks.text: Program.score is a class-level static field, initially 10. Main declares its own local score, initially 3.

blocks.title: Worked example · Resolve each name
blocks.text: The unqualified score inside Main refers to the local. Program.score explicitly selects the class field; the field has not changed.
